plan.notes: Source: official UMD 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog page 'Computer Science Major' (College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences) — https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/computer-mathematical-natural-sciences/computer-science/computer-science-major/ — transcribed by hand from the department's official term-by-term sequence, 'Computer Science - General Track, Effective Fall 2024' (https://undergrad.cs.umd.edu/sites/undergrad.cs.umd.edu/files/images/uploads/2024/04/2401%20Computer%20Science%20General%20Track.pdf), the plan the catalog's official 4-Year Plans hub (4yearplans.umd.edu) routes to. This is the newest published CS General Track plan (it supersedes the 2301/Fall-2023 version) and was still the current department plan on 2026-09-30. UMD awards a Bachelor of Science for this major; 'General Track' is the standard degree path (Cybersecurity / Data Science / Machine Learning / Quantum Information specializations are options, not the default degree). All course codes, titles, and credit hours are verbatim from the official documents; placeholders (CMSC 4XX, STAT 4XX, MATH/STAT/AMSC elective, Upper-Level Concentration, gen-ed slots) are student-choice per the official plan. The plan sheet is labeled 'This is a generalized academic plan, not an official audit'. Credits modeled at 120: Fall Year 2 uses a 4-credit MATH/STAT/AMSC slot (per the plan's '3 or 4' credit option) and Spring Year 4 uses a 3-credit free elective (per the plan's '3 or 4' option). Benchmark rules from the official plan: CMSC131, CMSC132, and MATH140 must be completed with C- or higher by 45 credits; CMSC330, CMSC351, and a MATH/STAT course must be completed with C- or higher by 75 credits. Prereqs recorded only where the official UMD sources state them: CMSC132 requires CMSC131 (official UMD plan note); CMSC250 requires CMSC131 and MATH141 (catalog course page); CMSC330 requires CMSC216 and CMSC250 (Fall 2026 CMSC330 syllabus); CMSC351 requires CMSC216 and CMSC250 (catalog course page); STAT 4XX and the MATH/STAT/AMSC elective require MATH141 (stated on the official plan sheet itself). Diversity footnote: two Distributive Studies courses approved for Big Question (SCIS) courses are required; Understanding Plural Societies (UP) and Cultural Competence (CC) may also fulfill Distributive Studies categories. Professional Writing may be any ENGL 39X course (e.g., ENGL 393 Technical Writing). Upper Level Concentration: minimum 12 credits of 300-400 level courses in one discipline outside CMSC, each course minimum 3 credits, 2.0 average required. Upper Level Electives: 6 credits from CMSC 300- or 400-level courses (excluding CMSC330 and CMSC351).
